scope: Windows x64 synthetic registered mode-1 party: original-DLL status, full result CSV and cumulative journal comparisons. All 35 zero-ID enemy skill slots are tested. One nonzero normal action with null conditions selects ENEMY1 (itself) at rates 100 and 0; RANDOM and four profession selectors damage the expected living neutral player at rate 100. Skill slots 1 through 14 separately target the mercenary and cause observed damage. Slot 1 is tested with normal slot 0 also registered, but both actions executing is not proven. Dead-member fallback, special and death slots, other skill targets and nonempty triggers are unverified or rejected. Twelve cases cover player effects and two waves. Actual C# NativeRegisteredBattle adapter is compiled/executed against the rebuilt DLL with original result/journal comparisons, configuring continue, end turn 20 and initial burst 40; end turn is asserted in output. One scenario consumes end_turn=0 from an isolated service response through CnProtocol and the managed adapter; other battle data are synthetic. A nonzero call-skill record is registered for each member via the managed adapter and original DLL; call-skill execution is not established. Continue and burst effects beyond matching results are not separately exercised. No real resources, Unity engine, ARM64 or iPhone execution was tested.
